hypothesis: At a 10-second prediction horizon, BTCUSDT order-flow features (book imbalance, aggressive trade imbalance, microprice deviation, depth pressure, regime state) combined with passive maker-queue execution (cost floor ~2 bps vs 14.5 bps taker) will produce statistically significant positive net EV. V12/V13 failed at 500ms/2s because (a) price moves are too small to overcome taker costs, and (b) taker execution cost 14.5 bps dwarfs the ~0-1 bps gross signal.
scientific_basis: V13 proved signal exists at 2s (AUC 0.72) but gross EV ~0 — 2s price moves too small
BTC 10s realized volatility ~0.05-0.10%% (~5-10 bps moves) — large enough to overcome maker costs
Binance Futures maker rebate: 0.02%% (2 bps received) vs taker fee 0.05%% (5 bps paid) — net 7 bps swing
Passive queue posting eliminates market-impact slippage for orders within visible queue depth
Order-flow persistence documented at 2-10s horizon (Cont & de Prado 2016; Bianchi et al. 2022)
data_source: Binance Futures BTCUSDT public WebSocket + REST (NEW real capture, V13 data excluded)

features.aggressive_trade_imbalance: signed buy/sell volume over window / total volume
features.microprice_deviation_bps: microprice distance from mid in bps
features.depth_pressure: recent cancel/add ratio at top of book
features.liquidity_state: depth available to absorb max trade in window

target_definition: 10s forward mid-price return in bps (regression); binary if return > transaction-cost breakeven

execution_assumptions.mode: passive maker-queue (primary), market taker (exit stop-loss only)

forward_period: NEW capture session #2, temporally after calibration (data/v14/forward/)
forward_data_contamination_rules: Forward capture session must start AFTER calibration session ends
Model frozen before any forward data is seen
